specification.title: Factors influencing adoption of digital learning among university students in South Africa
specification.problem: The proposed study will estimate digital learning adoption and examine student-level associations with perceived usefulness and access. The literature search must establish the specific contextual gap before claims of novelty or unmet need are accepted.
specification.field: Educational technology and digital learning adoption
specification.geography: South Africa; participating public universities will be selected after access and ethics approval
specification.population: Students aged 18 or older enrolled at participating South African public universities during 2027
specification.temporalScope: One survey wave in the 2027 academic year
specification.framework: Technology acceptance as a provisional conceptual lens linking perceived usefulness and facilitating access to adoption; definitions and theoretical claims require verified literature
specification.contribution: A bounded empirical estimate and exploratory association analysis in participating universities, conditional on a verified contextual research gap
specification.limitations: Cross-sectional self-report cannot establish causality; institutional participation and nonresponse limit generalisability; precision-based sampling does not guarantee power for every association
specification.scopeLimits: Adults enrolled at participating public universities; academic digital learning use only; no claim to cover all South African students
specification.institutionRequirements: No institutional template has been supplied; institutional compliance is not certified

questions.text: What proportion of eligible students report at least weekly use of digital learning tools for academic study?
How are perceived usefulness and reliable access associated with at least weekly digital learning use?

objectives.text: Estimate the proportion of eligible students reporting at least weekly academic digital learning use, with uncertainty intervals.
Explore associations of perceived usefulness and reliable access with at least weekly academic digital learning use.

constructs.name: Digital learning adoption
constructs.definition: Self-reported academic use of digital learning tools at least once per week in the preceding four weeks
constructs.scale: Binary: at least weekly versus less frequent

constructs.name: Perceived usefulness
constructs.definition: Agreement that digital learning supports the respondent's academic study; final item wording will be sourced and piloted
constructs.scale: Five ordered response categories from strongly disagree to strongly agree

constructs.name: Reliable access
constructs.definition: Self-reported availability of a suitable device and internet connection when needed for academic study
constructs.scale: Binary: reliable access versus access constraints

dataSources.name: Proposed anonymous student survey
dataSources.collectionMethod: An online questionnaire distributed through consenting participating universities; no data have yet been collected

analyses.method: Frequencies, adoption proportion and 95% confidence interval
assumptions: A documented probability sampling frame is available before recruitment
Response and coverage bias are examined
analyses.missingDataHandling: Report missingness and item-specific denominators; do not classify missing adoption responses as non-adoption

analyses.method: Exploratory binary logistic regression with usefulness coded as ordered-category indicators and reliable access as a binary predictor
assumptions: Independent observations or a justified adjustment for institutional clustering
Adequate outcome events for the proposed parameters
No complete separation or problematic collinearity
analyses.missingDataHandling: Report complete-case counts and compare included and excluded cases; do not claim imputation without a documented plan

specification.hypothesisRationale: Exploratory association hypotheses correspond to the second objective; results will not be interpreted as causal effects or guaranteed adequately powered tests.

hypotheses.nullHypothesis: Perceived usefulness and reliable access have no association with at least weekly digital learning use in the specified model.
hypotheses.alternativeHypothesis: At least one proposed explanatory variable is associated with at least weekly digital learning use in the specified model.
hypotheses.plannedTest: Likelihood-ratio comparison of the proposed exploratory logistic model with an intercept-only model

sampling.frame: Proposed institution-maintained enrolment lists at participating universities, subject to access and ethics approval; no accessible frame is asserted yet
sampling.rationale: Planning assumption: conservative proportion 0.5 and 5 percentage-point precision at 95% confidence under independent probability sampling, with 80% response assumed for invitation planning. No finite population correction without an authenticated denominator. The design effect of 1 applies only to independent sampling; clustered recruitment requires revision before implementation. This calculation supports prevalence precision, not guaranteed power for the exploratory regression.

evidence.claim: A study of undergraduate students at a rural South African university found that their LMS experiences were shaped by infrastructural limitations, digital literacy gaps and variation in faculty engagement.
evidence.quote: The findings revealed that while students identified the opportunity for learning flexibility and access through the LMS, their experience was primarily shaped by infrastructural limitations, gaps in digital literacy, and variation in the level of engagement by faculty.
